Yeah.

Yeah.

segments.title: Recording setup and address at Summers' house
segments.summary: Interviewer tests the recorder and announces the date, November 11, 1963, at Eddie Summers' house.

segments.title: Birth in Port Island and his father the bass player
segments.summary: Summers was born September 15, 1903 across the river from Baton Rouge; his father L.M. Summers played string bass with several country bands.

segments.title: Coming to New Orleans and joining Kid Sheik's band
segments.summary: He came to New Orleans and his first band was George Colar's (Kid Sheik); they recall the six-piece lineup of drums, clarinets, banjo and bass.

segments.title: Jobs played and thirty-seven years with Sheik
segments.summary: The band played yard parties, dances and weddings; Summers has been with Sheik off and on about 37 years.

segments.title: How he met Sheik and the Texas-jacket uniform
segments.summary: Sheik met him on a streetcar and recruited him as the band's trombonist; they joke about the blue pants and Texas jackets and Sheik's sister.

segments.title: Playing with Kid Rena, George Augustin and Lawrence Tucker
segments.summary: He lists other bands he played with and recalls the George Augustin band personnel.

segments.title: Regular work and famous uniform of the 1927 band
segments.summary: Same kinds of jobs in the 1927 band; brief talk of the band's famous uniform.

segments.title: Trombone lessons with Vic Gaspard and Sonny Henry
segments.summary: He studied trombone with Vic Gaspard (longest) and Sonny Henry; a garbled stretch of the tape follows.

segments.title: Favorite trombonists Harrison Bradley and Boots Young
segments.summary: He took up trombone after seeing players, names Harrison Bradley and Albert 'Boots' Young as favorites, and says he sounds like Bradley and subbed for him in Kid Rena's band.

segments.title: Brass bands: Sonny Henry, Tuxedo and Eureka
segments.summary: Sonny Henry played with the Tuxedo brass band; Summers played mostly mixed bands in the 1920s and brass bands like Eureka from about 1938.

segments.title: Johnson Serenaders and later bands with Sheik
segments.summary: He recalls playing with a Johnson band whose drummer was Jule Hill, and eight years with Sheik; later he mostly played jump jobs.

segments.title: Navy band service 1942-45 and return to New Orleans
segments.summary: He played in the US Navy band in California and McAlester, Oklahoma from 1942 to 1945, then returned to his job at the Athletic Club and spot jobs.

segments.title: Anderson Minor and the Lawrence Tucker Oriental Serenaders
segments.summary: He played spot jobs and carnival parades with Anderson Minor, and recalls the lineup of the late-1920s Lawrence Tucker band, called the Oriental Serenaders.

segments.chapter: Vic Gaspard and the Lyric Theatre
segments.title: Jack Teagarden and early trombone solos
segments.summary: Summers claims he and Jack Teagarden, who lived in New Orleans and played the Palace Theatre, were first to play trombone solos, ahead of Tommy Dawson; they studied with Gaspard together.

segments.chapter: Vic Gaspard and the Lyric Theatre
segments.title: Vic Gaspard at the Lyric Theatre
segments.summary: Gaspard led a band at the Lyric Theatre; Summers hung around there with passes.

segments.chapter: Vic Gaspard and the Lyric Theatre
segments.title: Gaspard as strict musician, and lesson prices
segments.summary: Gaspard taught by music, not jazz; he charged Summers a dollar and a quarter for about two hours.

segments.title: Back with Sheik after the war; band members
segments.summary: After California he rejoined Sheik's band, with Howard, Big Art on drums, Smitty on piano and Joe Morris on bass, about 1948.

segments.title: Tulane and Kid Howard recordings
segments.summary: The Tulane record came from a regular band; no earlier recordings; he did little with Howard, whose record men were picked by Ken Mills.

segments.title: Tight jams: fights and running from trouble at dances
segments.summary: Stories of a thrown cue ball, a beer bottle hitting Chester Zeno, and Melvin Frank and Joe Moyes running from shooting at a dance near Claiborne.

segments.title: Closing talk about the Texas jacket uniform
segments.summary: Wrap-up, with a return to the uniform of blue gingham Texas jackets with eye shades.
